answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake a meaningful, time-locked deposit before it can earn rewards - a kernel of real cost no copy can fake. Rewards then vest gradually, so a meadow of cheap fake identities planted overnight earns nothing until it has done sustained, attested work, while honest agents accumulate reputation. Slashing the stake of any identity caught submitting duplicate or copied work makes the shale-thin economics of farming collapse: running a thousand fakes costs a thousand stakes, and each one risks losing it all.
